growth_story.headline: A territory built on company registration and tourism, knocked down by the 2017 hurricanes and the pandemic, and recovering unevenly since.
growth_story.arc: The data file holds no record of income per person for the British Virgin Islands, so the tool finds no eras and cannot classify the growth problem. The sources tell the story instead: since the late 1970s the territory has built one of the world's leading centres for registering companies, and with tourism this is one of the economy's two main sectors. In September 2017 two of the strongest hurricanes on record, Irma and Maria, did damage larger than a full year's output and badly damaged the tourism sector's land and sea infrastructure. The pandemic then closed the borders in 2020; output fell again in 2021 and recovered only in part in 2022 as tourism and rebuilding picked up, while new company registrations dropped. In 2025 company registrations rose but stayover arrivals fell, and the latest regional review says the post-pandemic tourism rebound across the Caribbean had largely run its course.

threads.title: Company registry at the core
threads.text: Registering and managing companies for clients overseas is one of the two main sectors of the economy, alongside tourism. The firms that form and manage these companies also pay for much of the government: they bring in more than half of public revenue.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe a deep fall after the 2017 storms and the pandemic, then a partial recovery, but the data file holds no income per person series for any year, so none of these swings can be checked against the tool's own record or turned into eras.
